creator: Xiang Yue, Yuansheng Ni, Kai Zhang, Tianyu Zheng, Ruoqi Liu, Ge Zhang, Samuel Stevens, Dongfu Jiang, Weiming Ren, Yuxuan Sun, Cong Wei, Botao Yu, Ruibin Yuan, Renliang Sun, Ming Yin, Boyuan Zheng, Zhenzhu Yang, Yibo Liu, Wenhao Huang, Huan Sun, Yu Su, Wenhu Chen (IN.AI Research, University of Waterloo, The Ohio State University, Independent, Camegie Mellon University, University of Victoria, Princeton University)
description: A Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning Benchmark for Expert AGI, designed to evaluate multimodal models on massive multi-discipline tasks demanding college-level subject knowledge and deliberate reasoning.
name: MMMU
rai:annotatorDemographics: 50 college students (including coauthors) from various disciplines and subjects
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: To further control the quality of our data, we perform two steps of data cleaning. In the first stage, lexical overlap and source URL similarity are employed to identify potential duplicate problems. These suspected duplicates were then reviewed by the authors to identify and eliminate any duplications. The second stage involves distributing the problems among different co-authors for format and typo checking. In the third and final stage, the authors categorize the problems into four difficulty levels.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: A user-friendly web interface for data annotation and verification developed by Tianyu Zheng.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The annotators are instructed to adhere to copyright and license regulations, avoiding data from sites prohibiting copy and redistribution. The annotators are advised to select questions without immediately available answers, such as those with answers in separate documents or at the end of textbooks. All questions must contain one or more images, be written in English, and meet the college-level difficulty. The question should not be ambiguous and can be answered with one of the given options or a short answer.
rai:dataBiases: The manual curation process may carry biases, and the focus on college-level subjects might not be sufficient for testing Expert AGI.
rai:dataCollection: The questions in our benchmark were manually collected by a team of 50 college students (including coauthors) from various disciplines and subjects, drawing from online sources, textbooks, and lecture materials.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: online sources, textbooks, and lecture materials
rai:dataLimitations: The manual curation process may carry biases, and the focus on college-level subjects might not be sufficient for testing Expert AGI.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: In the first stage, lexical overlap and source URL similarity are employed to identify potential duplicate problems. These suspected duplicates were then reviewed by the authors to identify and eliminate any duplications. The second stage involves distributing the problems among different co-authors for format and typo checking. Approximately 10% of the problems, classified as very easy and not aligning with our design criteria due to their simplistic nature, are excluded from the benchmark.
rai:dataSocialImpact: It is of both intellectual and societal importance to closely monitor the progress towards Expert AGI. MMMU will stimulate the community to build next-generation multimodal foundation models towards expert artificial general intelligence.
rai:dataUseCases: Evaluate multimodal models on massive multi-discipline tasks demanding college-level subject knowledge and deliberate reasoning.
